title: Coastal Goan Prawn and Coconut Soup
summary: This vibrant seafood broth captures the coastal spirit of Goa through a delicate interplay of fresh tiger prawns, tamarind, and silky coconut milk. Built upon an aromatic foundation of mustard seeds, curry leaves, and toasted ground spices, the soup offers a balanced heat complemented by the tangy depth of dried kokum pods. Preparation begins with a fragrant prawn shell reduction that infuses the broth with rich maritime character before tender vegetables and fresh herbs are added. A final finish of cold-pressed coconut oil and crushed black pepper enhances the comforting, restorative qualities of the dish. Perfect for cool evenings, this soothing meal showcases the traditional flavors of western India in a modern, light presentation. Pair this broth with warm steamed rice or sourdough crusts to soak up every drop of spice-infused goodness. The multi-layered cooking approach guarantees that each spoonful delivers a harmonized taste of sweet seafood, sharp citrus notes, and lingering warm herbs. Experience a truly memorable staple of Indian coastal cuisine in your own kitchen today.

steps.step: Peel and devein the fresh tiger prawns carefully, setting aside all the shells and heads in a glass bowl for the broth.
Rinse the prawn shells under cold running water to clear away any remaining impurities or debris before cooking.
Heat one tablespoon of coconut oil in a wide heavy pot set over medium heat until shimmering lightly.
Add the reserved prawn shells to the hot pan and cook while stirring constantly until they turn bright pink.
Crush two cardamom pods and one cinnamon stick slightly using a heavy mallet to release essential oils.
Toss the crushed whole spices into the pot with the pink prawn shells and stir well for thirty seconds.
Pour five hundred milliliters of filtered water into the pot to submerge the seasoned roasted shells.
Bring the mixture to a lively boil over high heat while skimming off any foam that rises to the top.
Reduce the burner heat down to low, cover the pot tightly, and simmer gently for twenty minutes.
Pour the simmered mixture through a fine mesh strainer placed over a large glass bowl to collect broth.
Press down hard on the shells using the back of a large spoon to extract every drop of concentrated juice.
Discard the spent shells and whole spices after extracting all liquid, then set the hot stock aside.
Finely dice the red onion and set it aside on a clean cutting board for the upcoming aromatic paste base.
Mince three cloves of garlic along with an equal amount of peeled fresh ginger using a microplane grater.
Slit two green chillies lengthwise, keeping the seeds intact for an authentic level of regional heat.
Combine ground turmeric, chilli powder, coriander, and cumin in a small bowl with two tablespoons water.
Stir the ground spices and water thoroughly until a smooth paste forms with no dry pockets remaining.
Soak four pieces of dried kokum in half a cup of warm water for ten minutes to soften the dark skins.
Chop the roma tomato finely and keep it near the stovetop alongside the prepared spice mixture.
Season the cleaned tiger prawns lightly with a pinch of salt and a splash of lime juice in a medium bowl.
Cover the seasoned prawns with plastic wrap and place them inside the refrigerator until needed later.
Verify that all remaining ingredients are measured and ready on your workspace before beginning assembly.
Heat the remaining coconut oil in the pot over medium flame until shimmering gently across the bottom.
Add the yellow mustard seeds and cover the pot briefly until they finish popping completely in hot oil.
Toss in the fresh curry leaves and slitted green chillies, frying them for ten seconds until fragrant.
Add the diced red onion to the pot and cook until translucent and soft, stirring frequently for six minutes.
Stir in the minced garlic and ginger paste, cooking for one minute until raw raw aromas dissipate fully.
Pour the prepared ground spice paste into the pot and stir constantly to prevent scorching on the pot bottom.
Cook the spice paste for two minutes until tiny oil droplets begin to separate from the dark fragrant mixture.
Add the chopped roma tomatoes and cook until they soften completely and breakdown into a thick sauce.
Slowly pour in the strained home-made prawn stock while whisking constantly to integrate all the spiced layers.
Add the soaked kokum pieces along with their liquid and one tablespoon of dark tamarind paste.
Season the soup base with salt, coarse black pepper, and one teaspoon of crumbled natural jaggery.
Bring the liquid to a gentle boil, then lower the heat and simmer uncovered for ten full minutes.
Pour four hundred milliliters of rich coconut milk into the simmering pot while stirring gently.
Warm the coconut milk soup until small bubbles form around the rim, avoiding a hard boiling motion.
Remove the marinated prawns from the refrigerator and drop them carefully into the hot simmering soup.
Poach the prawns gently in the broth for four minutes until they turn opaque pink and curl tightly.
Sprinkle one teaspoon of fragrant garam masala over the soup surface and stir lightly to blend in.
Turn off the heat immediately to prevent overcooking the tender seafood floating in the broth.
Stir in fresh lime juice and finely chopped cilantro leaves to bring bright herbaceous notes to dish.
Ladle the hot prawn soup evenly into four deep warm serving bowls, making sure each gets equal prawns.
Garnish with extra fresh cilantro and serve immediately alongside warm rice or steamed crusty bread.
